claims.statement: The production Terraform root module at terraform/environments/production is the sole deployment entrypoint; it is split across per-concern files (kv.tf, d1.tf, workers-*.tf, web-*.tf, modal.tf, vercel.tf, e2b.tf, opencomputer.tf, daytona.tf, checks.tf, moved.tf, service-auth.tf) to keep Terraform addresses stable, and its state lives in an S3-compatible Cloudflare R2 bucket (open-inspect-terraform-state, key production/terraform.tfstate).

Fresh deployments require a two-phase apply: first with enable_durable_object_bindings = false and enable_service_bindings = false (creating workers and migrations without bindings), then with both true to attach the SESSION Durable Object and service bindings; DO class deletion instead requires bindings enabled with a new migration tag, enforced by a plan-time precondition in the cloudflare-worker module.

The Cloudflare provider is pinned to >= 5.16, < 5.20.0 because 5.20.0 regressed cloudflare_worker observability (it emits observability.traces.propagation_policy, failing with 403 on accounts without the trace propagation feature).

The Vercel provider validates its API token on init even when web_platform = 'cloudflare' and no Vercel resources exist, so the production module defaults vercel_api_token to a dummy 24-character token and vercel_team_id to 'unused'; the Terraform workflow renders the same dummy defaults when Vercel secrets are absent.

Every Worker is deployed through the cloudflare-worker module using the native 3-resource pattern (cloudflare_worker + cloudflare_worker_version + cloudflare_workers_deployment at 100%) with observability enabled at head sampling rate 1, which is what makes the Workers Telemetry API log querying (scripts/cf-logs.ts) possible.

The control-plane worker binds REPOS_CACHE KV, the D1 database as DB, the R2 media bucket as MEDIA_BUCKET, queue producer bindings (IMAGE_BUILD_FINALIZATION_QUEUE plus AUTOFIX_QUEUE/AUTOFIX_DLQ when the GitHub bot is enabled), SLACK_BOT/LINEAR_BOT service bindings when those bots are enabled, and the SESSION Durable Object.

The control-plane worker's cron triggers are ['* * * * *', '7,37 * * * *', '23 * * * *'] and must stay in sync with the scheduler, image-build scheduler (IMAGE_BUILD_SCHEDULER_CRON), and abandoned-draft-sweep constants so maintenance work actually runs.

The control plane receives access-control lists (ALLOWED_USERS, ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS, ALLOWED_EMAILS, ALLOWED_GITHUB_ORGS, UNSAFE_ALLOW_ALL_USERS), WEB_APP_URL/WORKER_URL, provider configuration, and OAuth client IDs as plain-text bindings; a complete OAuth client pair (GitHub or Google) is the provider-enablement declaration, and partial pairs are rejected by variable validation.

Control-plane secrets include BROWSER_AUTH_SECRET (bound from the legacy nextauth_secret input so secret rotation stays decoupled from the browser-auth cutover), TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY, REPO_SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY, PROVIDER_ACCOUNTS_ENCRYPTION_KEY, IMAGE_CALLBACK_TOKEN_PEPPER, per-service SERVICE_AUTH_SECRET_* keys, GitHub App credentials (the private key must be PKCS#8 format for Web Crypto import), OAuth client secrets, sandbox-provider credentials, and SLACK_BOT_TOKEN.

Per-service sig1 verification keys (SERVICE_AUTH_SECRET_WEB, _SLACK_BOT, _GITHUB_BOT, _LINEAR_BOT), the image-build callback pepper, and the provider-account encryption key are generated in Terraform state (random_password/random_bytes) and never operator-supplied; the provider-account key must remain unchanged after provider credentials are stored, with the remote Terraform state as the recovery source for a generated key.

Every deployment provisions the image-build finalization Queue and dead-letter Queue (even with enable_slack_bot = false), with a consumer on the control-plane worker at batch_size 1, max_retries 12, retry_delay 15 s; consequently the Cloudflare API token must include Queues: Edit before any upgrade that terraform apply provisions resources.

D1 migrations are applied by null_resource.d1_migrations, which re-runs bash scripts/d1-migrate.sh whenever the sha256 of the sorted migration SQL files changes; the script enforces NNNN_description.sql naming, fails on duplicate numeric prefixes, skips already-applied versions, and executes each pending migration atomically together with its _schema_migrations ledger insert in one wrangler d1 execute so failures roll back and lost responses are safe to retry.

When web_platform = 'vercel', the web module creates the Vercel project without a git_repository (deploys go through the deploy-web.yml GitHub Action, which pins Vercel CLI 58.4.0 and uses vercel pull/build/deploy --prebuilt --prod), wiring CONTROL_PLANE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SANDBOX_PROVIDER, branding variables, and the sensitive SERVICE_AUTH_SECRET.

A check block fails the plan when the Vercel-assigned production URL differs from the expected https://open-inspect-<deployment_name>.vercel.app pattern, because browser-auth redirects and cross-service references would silently break on a mismatch.

When web_platform = 'cloudflare' (OpenNext), Terraform builds the web with npm run build:cloudflare, writes a generated wrangler.production.toml (CONTROL_PLANE_WORKER service binding, ASSETS binding, workers_dev disabled when a custom domain is set), uploads SERVICE_AUTH_SECRET via scripts/wrangler-secrets.sh (which also deletes retired GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET/GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET/NEXTAUTH_SECRET), deploys with wrangler deploy, and attaches the custom domain when configured.

The Slack bot worker deploys with its own KV namespace, a CONTROL_PLANE service binding, a SLACK_COMPLETION_QUEUE producer binding plus a dead-lettered consumer (max_retries 1), and exactly one classifier credential chosen by classification_model: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for an Anthropic model or OPENAI_API_KEY for an OpenAI model (an Anthropic classifier reuses the deployment-wide key so existing deployments need no new variable); an OpenAI classifier with a bot enabled requires classification_openai_api_key or validation fails closed.

When enable_github_bot is true, Terraform provisions the GitHub autofix queue pair and attaches the consumer to the control-plane worker (max_retries 4, retry_delay 30 s) while the GitHub bot worker itself carries the GitHub App credentials, webhook secret, and its own sig1 secret; the control plane's AUTOFIX_QUEUE/AUTOFIX_DLQ bindings are read-only health metrics since Autofix production is owned by the GitHub bot.

Modal is deployed through a null_resource CLI wrapper because no Terraform provider exists: source files (modal-infra src, sandbox-runtime src, deploy scripts, pyproject.toml, uv.lock) are hashed for change detection, secrets are created first, and deploy.sh eagerly builds the sandbox image (uv run python deploy.py --build-sandbox-image) before running modal deploy.

For sandbox_provider = 'vercel', Terraform builds a managed base-runtime snapshot deterministically named openinspect-base-<source-hash-16> (create temp sandbox, upload packages/sandbox-runtime, install runtime and tooling, snapshot, stop) and passes the name as VERCEL_BASE_SNAPSHOT_NAME; vercel_base_snapshot_id is a manual fallback that skips managed builds, and the control plane resolves the name to the newest matching snapshot at spawn time.

For sandbox_provider = 'opencomputer', Terraform builds a declarative template deterministically named openinspect-runtime-<source-hash-16> from a hash of the sandbox-runtime and builder sources and binds the template name as OPENCOMPUTER_TEMPLATE; setting opencomputer_template pins a manual template and skips the managed build.

The E2B template module depends_on the control-plane worker (worker-first ordering): the new control plane can boot the old launcher-bearing template while an old control plane cannot boot a launcher-less template, so a failed template rebuild leaves a fully working system; the trade-off is a brief 404 window on first enablement or e2b_template_id rotation.

Terraform hard-fails plans that would deploy an unusable or unsafe configuration: at least one admission allowlist or explicit unsafe_allow_all_users; at least one complete OAuth sign-in pair; GitHub sign-in needs a GitHub-specific or provider-neutral admission rule; Google sign-in needs provider-neutral email/domain admission (GitHub usernames/orgs cannot admit Google identities); a custom domain requires web_platform = 'cloudflare' plus a non-empty zone id.

The Terraform GitHub Actions workflow (TF_VERSION 1.14.8; concurrency group per ref with cancel-in-progress: false so applies are never cancelled) runs terraform fmt/init -backend=false/validate plus terraform test on PRs and posts a plan comment (truncated to 60 KB, failures still posted), and on push to main or workflow_dispatch runs terraform apply -auto-approve in the production environment with every variable sourced from repository secrets via TF_VAR_*; when Cloudflare/R2 secrets are absent the entire workflow skips plan/apply (external contributors).

Before plan and apply the Terraform workflow runs terraform state pull and, only when the stored control-plane worker version migration tag is still 'v2', writes scheduler-do-retirement.auto.tfvars.json staging the SchedulerDO v2-to-v3 deletion (new tag v3, old tag v2, deleted class SchedulerDO) — so the release-specific migration is not a permanent default for fresh deployments, and a missing or empty state is validly treated as not v2.

Terraform tests (tests/auth_provider_configuration.tftest.hcl and tests/classifier_provider.tftest.hcl) run with mocked providers in CI and assert OAuth pair wiring into control-plane bindings, provider-account key passthrough and 32-byte base64 generation (rejecting malformed/31-byte/33-byte keys), and per-model classifier credential binding on both bots.

terraform output verification_commands emits the canonical post-deploy checks: control-plane /health, sandbox backend health (a Modal shim health URL; Daytona, Vercel, OpenComputer, and E2B use provider APIs directly and have no shim URL), web URL curl -I, and an unauthenticated /sessions request that must return 401; outputs also expose worker names/URLs, bot event URLs, the D1 id, KV ids, and the effective web_app_url (the real Vercel production URL when on Vercel).

Open-Inspect is single-tenant by design: all users share one GitHub App installation and can access any repository the App is installed on, so deployments must run behind org SSO/VPN, install the App only on intended repositories, and restrict sign-in via ALLOWED_USERS / ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS / ALLOWED_EMAILS / ALLOWED_GITHUB_ORGS.

New environments are created by copying environments/production, changing the backend key (e.g. staging/terraform.tfstate) and the environment variable, then applying; resources are suffixed by deployment_name (which must be globally unique for Vercel URLs), so multiple environments can coexist in one account.

The Cloudflare API token needs account-level Workers Scripts, Workers KV Storage, Workers R2 Storage, D1, and Queues Edit (Queues: Edit is required for durable image-build finalization provisioning; Workers Routes: Edit only when routes or custom domains are managed through Terraform).

scripts/cf-logs.ts queries the Workers Observability Telemetry Query API for historical logs by session id, Cloudflare request id, trace id, or free text (--json output for LLM debugging), requiring CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN with Workers:Read permission and CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID.

scripts/merge-split-users.ts converges a split canonical user pair (identities and Better Auth accounts, coding and browser sessions, automations, SCM tokens, read states) onto a survivor and deletes the emptied loser row; it is dry-run by default with --execute to apply and is idempotent, so partially-applied runs are repaired by re-running.
